identity.spiritualSignificanceShort: Ekambareswarar Temple is the earth shrine of the Pancha Bhuta Sthalams, the five Shiva temples of South India identified with the elements: here Shiva is worshipped as a Prithvi lingam. It is also a Paadal Petra Sthalam, praised in the seventh-century Tevaram hymns. The temple's sthala vriksham, an ancient mango tree under which the deity is said to have been worshipped, gives the temple its name and remains the focus of devotees' visits.

narrative.summaryIntro:
Ekambareswarar Temple in Kanchipuram, Tamil Nadu, is one of the most ancient temples dedicated to Lord Shiva and is particularly significant for its association with the ancient mango tree within its premises. The temple is one of the major temples in Kanchipuram and features impressive Dravidian architecture with a 150-foot high gopuram. The temple's name 'Ekambareswarar' refers to Shiva worshipped beneath the mango tree (Ekam means one, Ambara means mango tree).

The temple is known for its magnificent granite structures and elaborate stone carvings developed over multiple dynasties. The sacred mango tree is believed to be thousands of years old and holds immense spiritual significance. The temple attracts thousands of devotees and pilgrims, particularly during Maha Shivaratri and other major festivals. The site represents the continuity of Hindu spiritual tradition spanning centuries.
narrative.documentedHistory:
The HR&CE department describes Ekambaranathar as one of the oldest temples in Kanchipuram, estimating its age at more than 1,300 years and holding that it predates the Kailasanathar temple. Inscriptions in the complex span the Pallava through Nayaka periods.

The large Raja Gopuram over the southern gate was built by the Vijayanagara king Krishnadevaraya and carries an inscribed date of 1509. Wikipedia places his eleven-storey tower in the period 1509-29 and gives its height as 59 m (194 ft), among the tallest in South India; the Wikimedia Commons description of the same tower gives 55 m (180 ft). The Thousand Pillar Hall (Aayiram Kaal Mandapam) is also of the Vijayanagara period; the HR&CE page refers to an Ayrangal Mandapam, formerly called the Nootruka Mandapam.

The temple is one of the 276 Paadal Petra Sthalams venerated in the Tevaram, and the complex covers roughly 9.3 hectares.
narrative.sacredTree: Mango (the sthala vriksham). Temple tradition holds that its four branches yield four different kinds of mango and identifies them with the four Vedas; a traditional age of 3,500 years is often quoted but is not a scientific dating.

visitingInfo.officialContactNote: Same-day timings, pooja changes and festival arrangements should be confirmed with the HR&CE temple office on 96292-93020 or at hrce.tn.gov.in (temple id 1816).

openingHours.notes: HR&CE lists the morning session as 6:00 AM to 12:30 PM, with a stated afternoon closure from 1:00 PM to 4:00 PM; the half hour between 12:30 and 1:00 PM is not accounted for on the page.
HR&CE lists the evening session as 4:00 PM to 8:30 PM, although the same site schedules the Ardhajama pooja from 8:30 PM to 9:30 PM.

shrines.locationDescription: The main sanctum, housing the earth lingam of the Pancha Bhuta Sthalam series.
Shrine of the consort goddess within the complex.
The ancient mango tree from which the temple takes its name; tradition holds that its four branches bear four different varieties of mango, identified with the four Vedas.
The eleven-storey tower over the southern gate, built by the Vijayanagara king Krishnadevaraya and carrying an inscribed date of 1509; one of the tallest gopurams in South India.
A pillared hall of the Vijayanagara period. The HR&CE page refers to an Ayrangal Mandapam in the complex, formerly called the Nootruka Mandapam.
